newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fazio - Rome must keep up course of consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Fazio - Rome must keep up course of consolidation.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Friday that Rome needs to keep up its efforts to reduce budget deficits.
In a speech at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress, Fazio said "It will be necessary to maintain the present course of fiscal consolidation and moderation with respect to all incomes."
He said that he expected the average rate of inflation in 1997 would be kept between two and three percent.
Fazio also said that Rome needed to ensure healthy rates of investment.

"As progress is made in writing the public finances, policies to give a significant boost to investment appear increasingly necessary to take full advantage of Italy's considerable savings capacity," Fazio said.
Fazio said that a relatively wide fluctuation band around central parity is needed where economies are not sufficiently "homogeneous".
He said that for Europe to become an optimal currency area, it would be necessary to overcome still-considerable differences in productive structures, tax regimes and institutions.
He added that the cross-border mobility of goods and capital is high, but that mobility of labour is inadequate.
Fazio said that after a sharp upturn in inflation in 1995, monetary policy was now bringing inflation down.
